title: MeteoCore
description: MeteoCore OGC server. Summary first; then traffic, rendering, freshness, caches, memory and logs; then one row per engine. Rows open on demand, so closed rows run no queries. Panel descriptions say what each signal means and what bad looks like.

list.name: job
list.label: Job
list.description: Prometheus job scraping MeteoCore; every query is scoped to it so a shared Prometheus cannot mix in another service's http_* or process_* series.

list.name: collection
list.label: Collection
list.description: Collections that report any per-collection series. Filters the per-collection panels; global ones are unaffected.

list.name: api
list.label: API
list.description: The API label of the HTTP and render metrics (edr, features, maps, tiles, wms, 3dtiles, ...).

list.name: cache
list.label: Cache
list.description: Byte-bounded caches, discovered from every `<name>_cache_hits_total` family the server exposes; drives the cache table and the repeated per-cache cards.

panels.title: Collections
panels.description: Collections in `ready` state against those configured. Degraded and failed ones are the next two stats; /health names the reason, and the warnings log usually says why.

panels.title: Degraded
panels.description: Collections serving with reduced capability: database unreachable, empty catalog, a truncated station list, a broker session down. /health names the reason.

panels.title: Failed
panels.description: Collections that could not be built at all. A reload or the background retry may bring them back; the warnings log has the error.

panels.title: Stale feeds
panels.description: Collections whose newest data is older than 1.5 times their own peak age of the day before, and older than 15 min. Data age is a sawtooth with each feed's cadence, so a fixed threshold cannot fit a radar and a model run; yesterday's peak can. Collections younger than a day are not counted.

targets.expr: count((max by (collection) (collection_data_age_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}) > 1.5 * max by (collection) (max_over_time(collection_data_age_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[1d] offset 1d))) > 900) or vector(0)

panels.title: Requests/s
panels.description: HTTP requests per second over the last 5 min, for the APIs picked in API.

panels.title: 5xx ratio
panels.description: Share of responses with a 5xx status over the last 5 min, 503 load shedding included. Amber from 0.5 %, red from 2 %. Any sustained value is worth a look at the error log.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api", status=~"5.."}[5m])) or vector(0)) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[5m]))

panels.title: 503 shed /1h
panels.description: 503 responses in the last hour: requests turned away by render, decode or read admission (queue full, memory budget, deadline). Clients retry these, so a few are harmless; a steady stream means the server is short of render slots or memory.

panels.title: Latency p95 · p99
panels.description: HTTP latency over the last 5 min across the picked APIs (health and metrics excluded). Amber from 1 s, red from 3 s. Quantiles are unreliable below ~0.1 req/s.

panels.title: Render slots busy
panels.description: Render slots in use of `[server] render_concurrency`, shared by WMS, Maps, Tiles and 3D Tiles. Brief peaks are normal during animation; sitting at the top means renders queue.

panels.title: Render queue
panels.description: Requests waiting for raster memory or a render slot, as a share of the queue capacity. A full queue answers 503 at once.

panels.title: Render memory
panels.description: Share of the transient raster render budget (MC_RENDER_MEMORY_MB) reserved by renders in flight.

panels.title: Cold renders/s
panels.description: WMS, Maps and Tiles renders that had to read source data (render outcome `cold`) over the last 5 min, for the picked APIs and collections. This is the render cost that drives the latency tail.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Resident set size of the server process. Off Linux, where RSS is not read, this shows jemalloc resident bytes instead.

panels.title: Allocator overhead
panels.description: jemalloc resident ÷ allocated: physical pages held per byte the application uses. Healthy below 1.5×; the glibc fragmentation incident ran at ~3×.

panels.title: Egress
panels.description: Response bytes per second over the last 5 min, for the picked APIs.

panels.title: Remote reads
panels.description: Bytes per second read from S3/HTTP sources over the last 5 min, for the picked collections. Local-file collections read ~0.

panels.title: Requests by API
panels.description: Requests per second by API, stacked. A sudden change of shape usually means a client changed its configuration, not that the server did.

panels.title: Latency p95 by API
panels.description: p95 per API. Dashed lines mark 1 s and 3 s. Quantiles are unreliable below ~0.1 req/s: they interpolate to bucket tops from single samples, so check the request rate before believing a spike on a quiet API.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, api) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", api=~"$api", api!=""}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Errors & shedding
panels.description: 4xx = client mistakes (bad parameters, unknown collections). 5xx = server faults, read the error log. 503 = load shed by render, decode or read admission; it is part of 5xx in the ratio stat but drawn on its own here.

targets.expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api", status=~"5..", status!="503"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Requests by route — top 10
panels.description: The ten busiest route templates per step, for the picked APIs.

panels.title: Latency p50 · p95 · p99
panels.description: Request latency across the picked APIs. Pick API = wms for the WMS view: GetMap, GetCapabilities and GetFeatureInfo share the /wms route, so p50 is mostly warm hits and the p99 tail cold renders. The render alone, by outcome and collection, is in Rendering & admission.

panels.title: Latency p95 by route — top 10
panels.description: The ten slowest route templates per step, among routes serving at least 0.01 req/s (quieter routes only produce noise).

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, path) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", api=~"$api", api!=""}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (path) (sum by (path) (rate(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0.01))

panels.title: Errors by status code
panels.description: 4xx and 5xx responses per second by status code, stacked: 4xx in amber shades, 5xx in red shades, 503 shedding in purple.

panels.title: Routes
panels.description: Every route template over the dashboard's time range, for the picked APIs: requests, the share answered 4xx and 5xx, p95 and p99 latency, and bytes served. 5xx is amber from 0.1 % and red from 1 %; latency amber from 1 s and red from 3 s. Sort by any column.

targets.expr: (sum by (path, api) (increase(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api", status=~"4.."}[$__range])) or 0 * sum by (path, api) (increase(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__range]))) / sum by (path, api) (increase(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__range]))

(sum by (path, api) (increase(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api", status=~"5.."}[$__range])) or 0 * sum by (path, api) (increase(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__range]))) / sum by (path, api) (increase(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__range]))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, path, api) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__range])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, path, api) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Egress by API
panels.description: Response bytes per second by API, stacked. Responses without a known length are not counted (no handler streams).

panels.title: Served by API
panels.description: Bytes served per API over the dashboard's time range.

panels.title: EDR queries — rate by route
panels.description: EDR data routes only (position, area, radius, cube, trajectory, locations; metadata routes excluded): radar probes and point queries, lightning windows, station time series, vertical cross-sections.

panels.title: EDR queries — p95 by route
panels.description: p95 per EDR data route. A PVOL position resamples polar volumes (tens of ms warm, seconds after a remote fetch); a lightning area is one indexed SQL window (ms). A route drifting up under steady traffic is an engine or database regression, not client load.

panels.title: EDR queries — 4xx · 5xx by route
panels.description: 4xx on area routes includes the response-size budget (QueryTooLarge 400): usually a client widening its area, parameters or time window. Any 5xx is ours: read the logs.

panels.title: Render latency by outcome
panels.description: WMS GetMap, Maps map and Tiles map-tile render latency, from the rendered-cache lookup to the response, for the picked APIs and collections; p95 solid, p99 dashed. hit = rendered-cache hit (sub-ms), assembled = WMS view built from cached meta-tiles, cold = the engine read source data: the render a user actually waits for. Shed and expired renders are not here: see Shedding & deadlines.

panels.title: Render p95 by collection — top 10
panels.description: Which collection owns the render tail (cold and assembled; hits are sub-ms everywhere). One slow collection with the others flat points at its source (remote store, decode, overview choice), not at render admission. Click a series to filter the dashboard to it.

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, collection, outcome) (rate(render_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", api=~"$api", collection=~"$collection", outcome!="hit"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Render phases — p50
panels.description: Where a typical served render spends its time, by API and phase. queue = waiting for raster memory and a render slot; engine = get_raster_tile (source read, decode, reproject; summed over a WMS view's uncached meta-tiles); assemble = WMS meta-tile resample; encode = colorize + image encode. Hits run no phase. Phases carry no collection label, so the collection picker does not apply.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le, api, phase) (rate(render_phase_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Render phases — p95
panels.description: Where the slow renders spend their time. A rising queue line over a flat engine line means too few render slots (`[server] render_concurrency`); a rising engine line means a slow source. Expired renders are not here: see the stage split in Shedding & deadlines.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, api, phase) (rate(render_phase_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Render slots
panels.description: Slots in use against `[server] render_concurrency` (default 2× CPUs, min 8; fixed at boot). Flat at the top = renders queueing; brief touches are normal during animation bursts.

panels.title: Render queue
panels.description: Requests waiting for raster memory or a render slot, against MC_RENDER_QUEUE_CAPACITY (default 3× render concurrency). A full queue answers 503 at once.

panels.title: Render memory
panels.description: Transient output-buffer estimate (32 bytes per output pixel; composites add a plane per band) reserved by renders in flight, against MC_RENDER_MEMORY_MB. Separate from source decoding and resident caches.

panels.title: Shedding & deadlines
panels.description: Raster renders refused with 503 by the shared render executor, per minute. At once: queue full, or oversize (larger than the whole memory budget). Deadline by stage: queue = expired waiting for memory or a slot, render = expired after admission. `memory wait expired` is the part of the queue deadlines spent waiting for memory (dashed: already counted).

panels.title: Cold renders & meta-tile declines
panels.description: Render work per second. Meta-tiles rendered = meta-tile cache misses (decode + resample + colorize), the cost signal p99 spikes track. Declined = WMS views whose covering tile count exceeded the pixel-proportional budget and fell back to an uncached direct render; a sustained rate means clients send viewports outside the cacheable envelope. Cold renders = requests whose render read source data.

panels.title: Slow renders (> 0.5 s)
panels.description: Every slow WMS render log line, for the picked collections: layer, render time, time waiting for a slot (sem_wait), tiles and misses of a meta-tiled view, size, and the render path.

targets.expr: {job="meteocore"} |~ "slow WMS (meta-tile |direct )?render" | json | layer=~"($collection)(/.*)?" | line_format "{{.layer}}  {{.render_ms}} ms  sem_wait={{.sem_wait_ms}} ms  tiles={{.tiles}} misses={{.misses}}  {{.width}}x{{.height}}  ({{.message}})"

panels.title: Freshness
panels.description: Each collection's data age now, its peak age the day before, and the ratio. Data age climbs between deliveries and drops when new data lands, so a ratio well above 1 means the feed has stalled while the collection still reports ready. Amber from 1.5, red from 3; the Stale feeds stat counts the amber ones older than 15 min.

targets.expr: max by (collection) (collection_data_age_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}) / max by (collection) (max_over_time(collection_data_age_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[1d] offset 1d))

panels.title: Data age by collection
panels.description: Seconds since the newest data each collection serves (/health data_age_secs): GeoTIFF newest timestep, QueryData and NetCDF newest run, BUFR newest report, satellite newest scan, nowcast anchor frame. A sawtooth with the feed's cadence is normal. Bad: a line climbing past its usual peak. Negative = the newest data lies in the future. Click a series to filter the dashboard to it.

panels.title: Remote reads by collection
panels.description: Bytes per second fetched from S3/HTTP sources (cold COG tiles, PVOL volumes, GRIB messages, NetCDF chunks). A burst on a PVOL collection is pixel-cache misses being fetched again (Radar row).

panels.title: Remote requests per host
panels.description: Requests to each rate-limited remote host (today the remote NetCDF sources): in flight, waiting for a permit, and the host's limit (dashed). Polls take at most 2 permits. A queue that stays up means requests wait on the host, and that wait counts against their deadline.

panels.title: Fetched by engine
panels.description: Bytes read from remote storage per engine type over the dashboard's time range.

panels.title: Fetched by collection — top 10
panels.description: Bytes read from remote storage per collection over the dashboard's time range.

panels.title: All caches
panels.description: One row per byte-bounded cache picked in Cache, over the dashboard's time range: hit ratio, misses per second (misses are work: decodes, renders, remote fetches), fill against the configured capacity, resident bytes and entries where the cache counts them. An LRU is meant to fill; 100 % is only a sizing signal when the hit ratio sags with it and misses rise. Per-collection caches follow the Collection picker; global caches always show. New `<name>_cache_*` families appear here without a dashboard change.

targets.expr: sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[$__range:1m])) / ((sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[$__range:1m])) + sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_misses_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[$__range:1m]))) > 0)

panels.title: Misses by cache — top 8
panels.description: Misses per second for the eight busiest caches: actual work (decodes, renders, remote fetches). A cache whose misses jump while traffic is flat is churning, not loaded.

panels.title: Fill by cache
panels.description: Resident bytes as a share of each cache's configured capacity.

panels.title: ${cache}
panels.description: One card per cache picked in Cache (repeated): hit ratio and fill on the left axis, misses per second on the right. Healthy: a steady hit ratio. Fill pinned at 100 % is fine while the hit ratio holds; 100 % with a sagging ratio and rising misses means the working set no longer fits. No line = no lookups in the window.

panels.title: Process memory
panels.description: Healthy: RSS ≈ jemalloc resident, and resident within ~1.5× of allocated (live application bytes). resident ≫ allocated = allocator retention or fragmentation. RSS ≫ jemalloc resident = memory outside the allocator (mapped files, thread stacks). Swap > 0 = host memory pressure. `caches` is the sum of every byte-bounded cache, the floor the process cannot go below. retained growing without allocated = arena fragmentation. RSS and swap are read on Linux only.

panels.title: Memory now
panels.description: A snapshot of the same accounting: RSS, allocator resident and live allocations, the bytes held by caches, and the transient bytes admission budgets have reserved.

panels.title: Cache memory by cache
panels.description: Resident bytes per cache, stacked: where the cache part of RSS goes.

panels.title: Admission budgets — use
panels.description: Transient memory reserved against each admission budget: render (MC_RENDER_MEMORY_MB), GeoTIFF decode (MC_GEOTIFF_DECODE_MEMORY_MB), Zarr read (MC_ZARR_READ_MEMORY_MB), NetCDF field read (MC_NETCDF_READ_MEMORY_MB), station-grid compute (MC_STATION_GRID_MEMORY_MB). These are admission estimates, not measured RSS; a request that does not fit is answered 503.

panels.title: Admission budgets
panels.description: Each budget's reserved bytes now, its capacity, the use, and requests it rejected over the dashboard's time range (oversize and expired memory waits for render).

panels.title: Admission rejections
panels.description: Requests turned away (503) per minute by each memory budget. Admission fails at once rather than waiting while it holds a render slot, except render memory, which waits in the render queue until its deadline.

panels.title: Requests by API & query type
panels.description: From the request logs: requests per second by API and query type (both Loki labels). Health and metrics requests carry no API and are left out.

panels.title: Error responses by status class
panels.description: From the request logs: 4xx and 5xx responses per second.

panels.title: Requests by collection — top 10
panels.description: From the request logs, which carry the collection id that the HTTP metrics deliberately do not: the ten busiest collections. Parses every request line, so wide time ranges are slow.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (collection) (rate({job="meteocore", api=~"$api", api!=""} | json collection="collection" | collection!="" | collection=~"$collection" [$__auto])))

panels.title: Warnings & errors
panels.description: WARN and ERROR events (not request lines): failed or degraded collections, reload problems, poll and source errors. With collections picked, only lines naming one of them.

panels.title: Error responses
panels.description: Request log lines answered 4xx or 5xx, with the error reason the API attached.

targets.expr: {job="meteocore", status_class=~"4xx|5xx", api=~"$api"} | json | collection=~"$collection" | line_format "{{.method}} {{.path}} → {{.status}} ({{.duration_ms}} ms) {{.error}} {{if .query}}?{{.query}}{{end}}"

panels.title: Recent requests
panels.description: All request log lines, newest first. Expand a line for every field; request_id matches the X-Request-ID response header.

targets.expr: {job="meteocore", api=~"$api"} | json | collection=~"$collection" | line_format "{{.method}} {{.path}} → {{.status}} ({{.duration_ms}} ms) rid={{.request_id}} {{if .query}}?{{.query}}{{end}}"

panels.title: PVOL pixel cache — churn
panels.description: The pre-warm keeps every advertised timestep's lowest-sweep default quantity resident, if it fits. Sustained inserts while entries sit flat at capacity = churn: pre-warmed frames are evicted and the next animation pays burst re-reads from storage. Fix: raise MC_PVOL_PIXEL_CACHE_MB to about twice the working set (sites × window ÷ cadence × one sweep). Read failures = moments that degraded to nodata (missing file, decode failure).

panels.title: PVOL pixel cache — resident
panels.description: Resident bytes against MC_PVOL_PIXEL_CACHE_MB, and the entry count (right axis).

panels.title: Radar & 3D caches — hit ratio
panels.description: ODIM composite (full HDF5 decodes), PVOL pixel, voxel-grid (polar resamples for 3D meshes), storm-cell set (segmentations) and 3D Tiles encoded-content caches.

panels.title: Radar & 3D caches — fill
panels.description: Resident bytes as a share of each cache's capacity.

panels.title: Lead-1 skill vs persistence
panels.description: Realized 5-min skill: each generation scores the previous one's lead-1 prediction against the fresh analysis (CSI), next to the persistence baseline (dashed). The nowcast must sit above its baseline; a collapsing gap = motion or source-data regression.

panels.title: Generation duration
panels.description: Wall-clock of the newest generation. It must stay well under the source cadence (300 s for a 5-min composite, the red line); above it, generations queue and the served time axis lags reality.

panels.title: Generations & failures per hour
panels.description: Generations in the trailing hour: ~12 at a 5-min source cadence; dips = skipped source frames. Any failure deserves a log read (the engine serves the previous generation meanwhile).

panels.title: Source lag
panels.description: Age of the source anchor frame when the generation finished: upstream latency plus generation time. Sustained growth = the source stalled, and every future frame goes stale with it.

panels.title: Retention
panels.description: Retained generations (the reference-time pinning window; resident memory multiplies with it) and frames (analysis + leads) in the newest generation.

panels.title: Cell tracker per hour
panels.description: Association bookkeeping in the trailing hour. Births and deaths above real cell turnover mean dropouts; pass-2 matches are the raw-position fallback (see the share); velocity clamps are jumps the tracker already rejected as motion. On quiet weather all sit at zero.

panels.title: Pass-2 share of matches
panels.description: pass-2 ÷ (pass-1 + pass-2) over the trailing hour. Pass 2 rescues counter-flow cells and also completes identity swaps; a rising share with steady cell counts is the first sign of swaps between co-located echoes. Empty when nothing matched.

targets.expr: sum by (collection) (increase(nowcast_cell_pass2_matches_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[1h])) / ((sum by (collection) (increase(nowcast_cell_pass1_matches_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[1h])) + sum by (collection) (increase(nowcast_cell_pass2_matches_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[1h]))) > 0)

panels.title: Gridded sources — GRIB, Zarr, NetCDF, GeoTIFF
Per-collection caches
panels.description: Caches kept per collection, over the dashboard's time range: GeoTIFF compressed tiles (tile_cache), GRIB decoded grids (grid_cache) and compressed messages (grib_message_cache; its hits measure reuse after grid misses, and its misses need storage reads), Zarr decoded chunks (zarr_decoded_cache; single-flight waiters count as hits). GRIB budgets are per source: grid_cache_mb and message_cache_mb.

targets.expr: sum by (cache, collection) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(tile_cache|grid_cache|grib_message_cache|zarr_decoded_cache)_hits_total", collection=~"$collection"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[$__range:1m])) / ((sum by (cache, collection) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(tile_cache|grid_cache|grib_message_cache|zarr_decoded_cache)_hits_total", collection=~"$collection"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[$__range:1m])) + sum by (cache, collection) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(tile_cache|grid_cache|grib_message_cache|zarr_decoded_cache)_misses_total", collection=~"$collection"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[$__range:1m]))) > 0)

sum by (cache, collection) (label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(tile_cache|grid_cache|grib_message_cache|zarr_decoded_cache)_bytes", collection=~"$collection"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_bytes")) / (sum by (cache, collection) (label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(tile_cache|grid_cache|grib_message_cache|zarr_decoded_cache)_capacity_bytes", collection=~"$collection"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_capacity_bytes")) > 0)

panels.title: Per-collection cache hit ratio
panels.description: Hit ratio per cache and collection. A ratio sagging while the cache's fill stays at 100 % means the working set no longer fits its per-source budget.

targets.expr: topk(12, sum by (cache, collection) (rate(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(tile_cache|grid_cache|grib_message_cache|zarr_decoded_cache)_hits_total", collection=~"$collection"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[$__rate_interval:15s])) / ((sum by (cache, collection) (rate(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(tile_cache|grid_cache|grib_message_cache|zarr_decoded_cache)_hits_total", collection=~"$collection"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[$__rate_interval:15s])) + sum by (cache, collection) (rate(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(tile_cache|grid_cache|grib_message_cache|zarr_decoded_cache)_misses_total", collection=~"$collection"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[$__rate_interval:15s]))) > 0))

panels.title: Per-collection cache misses
panels.description: Misses per second per cache and collection: decodes (grid, Zarr chunk) and storage reads (GeoTIFF tile, GRIB message).

panels.title: NetCDF detached field fills
panels.description: Cold remote NetCDF fields are fetched by a task the request hands its fill to; it finishes after the request's deadline and leaves the field cached. Pending = running now (at most 16). Inline = fills a request ran itself because 16 were running; a steady inline rate means fetches cannot keep up with the frames asked for. EDR and GetFeatureInfo reads use a pool of their own and are not counted.

panels.title: Per-collection cache memory
panels.description: Resident bytes per cache and collection, stacked.

panels.title: Scan windows vs scan cache
panels.description: Bytes of the scans in each satellite collection's time window, the part held in memory, and MC_SATELLITE_FRAME_CACHE_MB (dashed). Bad: all windows above capacity (the poll logs a WARN and stops downloading back), or resident below window for more than a poll or two: requests then download scans within the render deadline, and an animation's older frames answer 503.

panels.title: Scan downloads per hour
panels.description: Scans downloaded again by a poll after the scan cache evicted them, and scans a request had to download (scan-cache misses), in the trailing hour. Once the windows fit, request fetches stay near 0; a steady re-download rate means the windows barely fit.

panels.title: Stations behind the latest analysis
panels.description: Stations the latest analysis of each station-grid parameter was computed from: the first thing to check when an analysis looks wrong. A drop means the source lost stations and the field is interpolated from fewer, farther ones; 0 draws an empty map.

panels.title: Analyses, failures & duration
panels.description: Analyses in the trailing hour (request misses plus the poll's pre-compute and revisions), failed analyses and source reads, analyses rejected (503) because MC_STATION_GRID_MEMORY_MB was full, and the last analysis's duration (right axis). A duration near the 3 s render deadline means cold map requests answer 503 until the pre-compute catches up.

panels.title: Station-grid cache
panels.description: Hit ratio of the shared analysis cache and its fill against MC_STATION_GRID_CACHE_MB. Every revision of the observations re-keys a collection's grids, so a burst of misses after a late report is expected; a low ratio otherwise means the cache holds fewer grids than the maps animate over.

panels.title: Computation admission
panels.description: Bytes reserved by analyses being computed, against MC_STATION_GRID_MEMORY_MB (dashed).

panels.title: Database reachable
panels.description: Per collection, the latest 30 s SELECT 1 ping. Down = the collection is degraded in /health. Click a row to filter the dashboard to it.

panels.title: Collections down
panels.description: PostGIS collections whose latest ping failed.

panels.title: Truncated lists
panels.description: Collections whose cached station list was cut at `[postgis] max_locations`: stations past the cap are missing from /locations, Features and, in the observation-derived modes, from position and area. In mode B a cut station registry counts too. /health shows them degraded. Should be 0: raise max_locations or narrow the station set.

panels.title: Connection pool
panels.description: Per pool: open connections against capacity (dashed), connections acquirable now, and tasks waiting (amber). Sustained waiting > 0 = pool too small or slow queries.

panels.title: Pings & metadata refreshes
panels.description: In the trailing hour: failed pings (flip /health) and failed metadata refreshes (the previous snapshot is kept, so locations go stale), next to the totals so a flat zero failure line is not mistaken for nothing running. Right axis: the slowest last metadata refresh.

panels.title: Broker session
panels.description: Per collection: connected and subscribed to the WIS2 Global Broker, or reconnecting. /health degrades after degrade_after_secs. Click a row to filter the dashboard to it.

panels.title: Notification age & lag
panels.description: Age = seconds since the last accepted notification; it climbs between publications (MeteoAlarm is sporadic, SYNOP bursts at H+20). Lag = receipt − pubtime of the last one: seconds normally; a growing lag means the broker is replaying a backlog after a reconnect.

panels.title: Notifications per minute
panels.description: Accepted vs dropped by reason. Every notification is republished once per Global Cache, so dropped·duplicate ≈ 5× accepted is the healthy shape. Any other reason growing is a problem: parse = non-WNM payloads, policy = a link failed the download policy, integrity = checksum mismatch, size = over max_download_bytes, download = HTTP failures, decode = bad inline payload.

targets.expr: sum by (collection) (rate(wis2_messages_received_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[5m]) * 60) - sum by (collection) (rate(wis2_messages_dropped_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[5m]) * 60)

panels.title: Downloads, reconnects & unverified
panels.description: In the trailing hour. Downloads are needed only for link-only notifications (most SYNOP arrives inline). Reconnects should be rare; a steady rate means the broker keeps closing the session (keep-alive, session expiry, client id collisions). Unverified = sha3-* checksums accepted without checking.

panels.title: CAP alerts
panels.description: active = alert areas in the served catalog after Update/Cancel resolution (every source mode); held = alerts in the WIS2 accumulator. Right axis, trailing hour: superseded by a reference chain; evicted = expired past retention_grace or over max_alerts; evicted valid = still-valid alerts the max_alerts cap pushed out (should be 0).

panels.title: CAP over WIS2 — documents & geometry hints
panels.description: In the trailing hour. Documents: ingested, rejected (unparseable XML: a producer problem), deleted. Geometry hints (MeteoAlarm rel=geometry zone polygons): attached, or rejected (link expired, not a polygon, outside the notification bbox). A rising rejected share means alerts render without geometry.

panels.title: BUFR store
panels.description: Stations and reports held after pruning (retention × max_stations); reports on the right axis. A global SYNOP subscription levels off around 20 k stations × 24 hourly rows; a step down is a prune or a rebuild on reload. Flat at 0 with a ready collection = the source is empty or every report is out of the window.

panels.title: BUFR ingest per hour
panels.description: In the trailing hour: files or payloads fetched; reports ingested (new station-time rows), replaced (corrections), out_of_window (clock skew or a stale feed), skipped (no station id, position or time); decode failures by kind (error = malformed BUFR, unsupported = a decoder gap: a steady rate from one centre means its template needs the decoder extended); failed source scans.
